title: Copperwave Clinic — Inference Savings runbook (before/after Optimize)
content:
Context:
Copperwave Clinic is a mid-size telehealth provider running clinical summarization and patient triage models. They asked for a before/after savings projection comparing their current setup to applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization, smart batching, and KV prefix caching). This doc is a compact runbook for the CS + Solutions team with the model-level assumptions, baseline calculations, sensitivity checks, and a staged rollout checklist.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Baseline monthly inference spend estimated at $38,600 for production traffic (approx 120M tokens/month). After applying Redwood Optimize recommended changes (FP16->4-bit quant, per-route batching, KV prefix caching on triage flows) we project a baseline-adjusted monthly run rate of $14,900 (approx 61% savings). Realizable savings in first 90 days are expected to be 45–55% due to conservative rollout and monitoring. Key risks: model quality regressions at extreme quantization on long-consult transcripts and unexpected tail-latency from batching misconfiguration.

Assumptions and inputs (baseline):
- Production traffic: 120,000,000 tokens / month (combined prompts + responses)
- Current average latency target: 300ms p50, 1s p95
- Current model variant: distilled-clinical-v1 (FP16) on p4d instances (shared hosted)
- Current effective tokens-per-second: 60 tps per GPU on avg workload shapes (short triage + medium summaries)
- Baseline unit cost observed from billing: $0.322 per 1k tokens (includes infra + orchestration + margin)
- Current monthly spend: 120M tokens / 1k * $0.322 = $38,640

Optimize recommendations applied in model runbook: 1) 4-bit quantization with per-layer calibration for distilled-clinical-v1-q4; 2) Smart batching with dynamic batch caps (30 for triage short requests, 8 for long transcripts) and latency SLO-aware batching; 3) KV prefix caching for repeated patient context (estimated cache hit 18%); 4) Route-level model routing: cheap-summary variant for non-critical summaries (20% of summary volume).

Projected after-Optimize breakdown (conservative):
- Quantization delta: token execution CPU/GPU time reduced ~2.8x -> compute cost reduction 58%
- Batching & orchestration delta: effective utilization improves 1.6x -> additional 18% reduction
- KV prefix cache: reduces tokens executed by 18% on cacheable routes -> effective token volume falls from 120M to 98.4M
- Route-level cheaper model substitution: 20% of summaries diverted to cheap-summary at 0.12x cost of main model -> blended cost reduction 9%

Stepwise calculations (rounded):
1) Post-cache token volume = 120M * (1 - 0.18) = 98.4M tokens
2) Effective per-1k-token compute cost after quantization and batching = baseline $0.322 * (1 - 0.58) * (1 - 0.18) ≈ $0.322 * 0.42 * 0.82 ≈ $0.110 per 1k tokens
3) Adjust for cheap-summary substitution (assume 20% of summaries = 12% of total tokens): blended cost modifier ~ (0.88*1 + 0.12*0.12) ≈ 0.896. Apply: $0.110 * 0.896 ≈ $0.099 per 1k tokens
4) Projected monthly spend = 98.4M / 1k * $0.099 ≈ $9,742
5) Add estimated orchestration & reserved capacity uplift (to meet SLOs) + planned safety margin = +53% -> final monthly run rate ≈ $14,900

Comparative metrics: 
- Baseline monthly: $38,640
- Projected (post-Optimize conservative): $14,900
- Nominal point estimate savings: $23,740 / month (~61% raw, ~39% conservative realized first 90d)

Sensitivity scenarios (3 key toggles):
1) Quantization efficacy +/- 10% of compute reduction: range monthly $12.6k–$17.8k
2) Cache hit 10%–25%: range monthly $13.9k–$16.8k
3) Batch misconfiguration (suboptimal batch caps causing 10% lower utilization): increases monthly by ~$1.4k
Combined worst-case (conservative): $18.2k/month (still ~53% reduction vs baseline).

Quality safety checks (prioritized):
- Automated prompt/eval suite on critical intents (diagnosis mention, triage escalation) to detect regressions immediately after quantization PR.
- Shadow A/B: send 20% of live traffic to quantized + cached path for 7 days, compare NLU metrics and hallucination incidents.
- Latency SLO gates: if p95 > 2x baseline or error rate increases >0.5pp, auto-revert routing to FP16.

Rollout plan (3-week pilot -> 12-week gradual):
- Week 0: bench quantized variant offline with full calibration and per-layer fallback. Create canary model tag and inference config.
- Week 1: Internal load test with replayed traffic (1B tokens replay) + cost regression simulation. Verify perf and per-token cost math.
- Week 2: Shadow deploy at 0% traffic for 48h with monitoring + eval suite. If OK, proceed.
- Weeks 3–6: Canary live traffic 5% -> 20% with weekly evaluation. Monitor quality metrics and billing anomalies.
- Weeks 7–12: Gradual ramp 20% -> 80% while enabling KV caching and batching rules in phases. Keep 20% of routes on fallback variant for sensitive flows.

Implementation checklist for Solutions Engineers (CS):
- [ ] Create quantized artifact and store model tag: distilled-clinical-v1-q4-2025-09
- [ ] Add per-route batching profile entries to Redwood Console; triage route cap=30, summary route cap=8
- [ ] Configure KV prefix cache for patient-meta route, set TTL=12h and warm cache using last-30d keys
- [ ] Set up shadow route and canary policy in Console; enable tracing hooks for canary
- [ ] Wire automated eval suite (Confluence CW-987) to CI -> webhook for regression alerts
- [ ] Book customer review meeting week 4 and present early metrics (cost, p50/p95, QA pass rate)

Customer-facing one-pager (for Copperwave execs):
- Headline: "Potential monthly inference cost reduction of up to 61% (conservative first 90 days: 45–55%)"
- Key actions: enable Redwood Optimize quantization + batching + KV cache; approve 12-week pilot; sign off on rollback gates
- Ask: 90-day pilot authorization, access to anonymized traffic replay for calibration, point-of-contact for quality signoff

Open questions & notes for follow-ups:
- Need confirmation of proportion of tokens attributable to summaries vs triage (customer telemetry disagrees with initial estimate; affects cheap-summary benefit).
- Confirm legal/data requirements for caching patient context keys (PII handling and KMS footprint).
- Run an offline end-to-end hallucination evaluation on 10k transcripts to quantify any quality delta from q4 calibration.

Appendix — quick numbers snapshot (copyable):
- Baseline tokens/month: 120000000
- Baseline cost per 1k: $0.322
- Baseline monthly spend: $38,640
- Cache hit: 18% -> post-cache tokens: 98,400,000
- Estimated per-1k after quant+batch: $0.099 (blended)
- Conservatively adjusted monthly run rate (safety margins): $14,900

Notes/voice in doc: this is a working draft intended for Solutions Engineers and CS to use when prepping the customer pilot proposal. Keep iterations in this doc; move final numbers to customer-facing one-pager after verification.
